kinds.password.label: Password policy
kinds.password.appliesTo: the NEXT password set in this realm and to nothing already stored
password.FIELDS.minLength.label: Minimum length
password.FIELDS.minLength.what: The shortest password this service will set, counted in characters (Unicode code points, so an emoji is one). The attribute is draft-behera-ldap-password-policy's. Twelve is the default; NIST SP 800-63B asks for at least 8, and 15 where a password is the only factor.
password.FIELDS.history.label: Previous passwords that may not be reused
password.FIELDS.history.what: How many of a person's PREVIOUS passwords are remembered and refused. The current password is always refused as well while this is above 0, so 5 means a new password may be none of the last six. 0 turns the rule off. The draft's attribute, with the draft's meaning. Each remembered password is kept as the hash it was already stored as (argon2id or scrypt), in pwdHistory on the person's own entry, and checking a new password costs one hash comparison per one remembered.
password.FIELDS.minSymbols.label: Minimum number of symbols
password.FIELDS.minSymbols.what: How many characters that are neither a letter, a digit nor whitespace a password must contain. 0 turns the rule off.
password.FIELDS.requireUppercase.label: Require an uppercase letter
password.FIELDS.requireUppercase.what: Whether a password must contain at least one uppercase letter, in any script.
password.FIELDS.requireDigit.label: Require a number
password.FIELDS.requireDigit.what: Whether a password must contain at least one decimal digit.
password.FIELDS.generatedLength.label: Length of a generated password
password.FIELDS.generatedLength.what: How long a password this service MAKES UP is — for a new user created from the console or /admin-api, an operator's Generate, and the product-mode bootstrap account. It must be at least the minimum length and at least twice the symbol count plus two. Twenty characters from a 90-character alphabet is about 130 bits.
password.FIELDS.hashAlgorithm.label: Password hash algorithm
password.FIELDS.hashAlgorithm.what: The algorithm a newly stored password is hashed with: scrypt (RFC 7914), the default, or argon2id (RFC 9106, the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet's first choice). A stored hash names its own algorithm and parameters and keeps verifying; one that is not in this algorithm with these parameters is hashed again at the person's next verified sign-in. Client secrets, activation tokens, recovery codes and app passwords are not passwords and stay scrypt.
password.FIELDS.argon2Memory.label: argon2id memory
password.FIELDS.argon2Memory.what: The memory one argon2id hash uses, in kibibytes (m). 19456 KiB (19 MiB) is OWASP's minimum and the least this service will write. Raising it makes a stolen store slower to attack, and every sign-in uses that much more memory.
password.FIELDS.argon2Iterations.label: argon2id iterations
password.FIELDS.argon2Iterations.what: How many passes argon2id makes over its memory (t). 2 is OWASP's minimum at 19 MiB; each pass adds the same time again.
password.FIELDS.argon2Parallelism.label: argon2id parallelism
password.FIELDS.argon2Parallelism.what: How many lanes argon2id divides its memory into (p). It is part of the hash, not a thread count: node computes a hash on one thread whatever this says. 1 is OWASP's figure.
password.FIELDS.scryptLogN.label: scrypt cost (log2 of N)
password.FIELDS.scryptLogN.what: scrypt's CPU and memory cost for a newly stored password while the algorithm is scrypt, as a power of two: 15 (the default) is N=32768. OWASP's table pairs it with the parallelism: 2^17 with p=1, 2^16 with p=2, 2^15 with p=3, 2^14 with p=5, or 2^13 with p=10. The default, 2^15 with p=1, is below it.
password.FIELDS.scryptBlockSize.label: scrypt block size (r)
password.FIELDS.scryptBlockSize.what: scrypt's block size for a newly stored password while the algorithm is scrypt. Memory is about 128 × N × r bytes; 8 is the figure RFC 7914 and OWASP give.
password.FIELDS.scryptParallelism.label: scrypt parallelism (p)
password.FIELDS.scryptParallelism.what: scrypt's parallelism for a newly stored password while the algorithm is scrypt. Node computes it on one thread, so a higher value costs time rather than cores; the cost's description lists the pairs OWASP accepts.

kinds.authn.label: Authentication policy
kinds.authn.governs: which mechanisms are accepted as a first and as a second factor
kinds.authn.appliesTo: the NEXT sign-in in this realm; a session already started keeps the factors it was started with
kinds.authn.fallsBackTo: the default realm's profile where it has one, and the built-in defaults where it has not
authn.FIELDS.requireSecondFactor.label: Second factor required
authn.FIELDS.requireSecondFactor.what: `if-held`: a person is asked for a second factor when they hold one (or their entry says stsMfaRequired). `always`: everybody in this realm is, and somebody who holds none is sent to enrol one at their next sign-in. This replaced authn.mfaRequired. There is no "never": a held factor is always asked for.
authn.FIELDS.requireSecondFactorForAdmin: For anybody holding a console role (Admin Read or Admin Write) who holds no second factor. `offer`: they are shown the step that sets one up, with an Ignore button, at every sign-in. `always`: they must set one up before they are signed in — except the default realm's built-in administrator (admin.bootstrapUsername), who is only ever offered one, so a service is never left with nobody who can sign in. `if-held`: as everybody else, by the field above. WEAKER THAN `always`: an administrator on a password alone is an administrator anyone with the password is.
authn.FIELDS.passwordPrimary.label: Password — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.passwordPrimary.what: A password on the sign-in screen. As a SECOND factor it is the password asked for after a wallet or other passwordless first factor.
authn.FIELDS.passwordSecondFactor.label: Password — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.passwordSecondFactor.what: A password on the sign-in screen. As a SECOND factor it is the password asked for after a wallet or other passwordless first factor.
authn.FIELDS.passkeyPrimary.label: Security key or passkey (passwordless) — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.passkeyPrimary.what: A WebAuthn credential enrolled in the primary role, signing in with no password.
authn.FIELDS.securityKeySecondFactor.lab: Security key (second factor) — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.securityKeySecondFactor.wha: A WebAuthn credential enrolled in the mfa role, asked for after a first factor.
authn.FIELDS.totpSecondFactor.label: Authenticator app (TOTP) — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.totpSecondFactor.what: An RFC 6238 one-time code. Never a first factor: this service holds the same shared secret the app does. Off here, nobody may ENROL one; a person who already holds one is still asked for it, because an off switch that downgraded every enrolled account to a password alone would do something other than it says (this row replaced totp.enabled, and keeps its contract).
authn.FIELDS.recoveryCodeSecondFactor.la: Recovery code — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.recoveryCodeSecondFactor.wh: A single-use code from a set the person generated. Off here, no new set may be generated; a set already held still works (this row replaced backupCodes.enabled, and keeps its contract).
authn.FIELDS.emailCodePrimary.label: Emailed six-digit code — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.emailCodePrimary.what: A six-digit code mailed to the person's VERIFIED address. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeSecondFactor.label: Emailed six-digit code — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeSecondFactor.what: A six-digit code mailed to the person's VERIFIED address. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.
authn.FIELDS.emailLinkPrimary.label: Emailed sign-in link — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.emailLinkPrimary.what: A single-use link mailed to the person's VERIFIED address, which completes the sign-in only in the browser that started it. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. Off by default for that reason; turn it on only where that is an accepted risk.
authn.FIELDS.emailLinkSecondFactor.label: Emailed sign-in link — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.emailLinkSecondFactor.what: A single-use link mailed to the person's VERIFIED address, which completes the sign-in only in the browser that started it. NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.1: "Email SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication", because a mailbox may be reached with a password alone, and mail may be read in transit or rerouted. authn.FIELDS.certificatePrimary.label: TLS client certificate — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.certificatePrimary.what: A verified TLS client certificate: GET /tls/sign-in, or Continue with your certificate on the sign-in screen.
authn.FIELDS.kerberosPrimary.label: Kerberos (SPNEGO) — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.walletPrimary.label: Wallet presentation — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.walletPrimary.what: /authn/wallet with a credential this realm issued, or a SIOPv2 self-issued ID Token from an enrolled key. As a SECOND factor, the wallet presented after a password.
authn.FIELDS.walletSecondFactor.label: Wallet presentation — as a second factor
authn.FIELDS.walletSecondFactor.what: /authn/wallet with a credential this realm issued, or a SIOPv2 self-issued ID Token from an enrolled key. As a SECOND factor, the wallet presented after a password.
authn.FIELDS.federationPrimary.label: Federation partner — as a first factor
authn.FIELDS.federationPrimary.what: A sign-in asserted by a configured federation partner.
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeTtlS.label: How long an emailed code or link is valid
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeTtlS.what: From the moment it is sent. At most ten minutes, NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.1.3.2's bound for an out-of-band secret.
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeAttempts.label: Wrong codes before the sign-in step ends
authn.FIELDS.emailCodeAttempts.what: How many wrong codes one sign-in step accepts before it is ended and the person starts again. The per-person and per-network rate limits apply as well.
authn.FIELDS.emailResendS.label: Shortest wait before another code or link is sent
authn.FIELDS.emailResendS.what: A new code or link replaces the last one, which stops working. At most three are sent for one sign-in step.
authn.FIELDS.emailFailureLimit.label: Consecutive failures before a person's email factor is turned off
authn.FIELDS.emailFailureLimit.what: NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 3.2.2 asks for no more than 100. The person, and their administrators, are told, and the person turns it on again from the portal.
authn.FIELDS.rememberedBrowserSkipsSecon: A remembered browser may skip the second factor

OFF BY DEFAULT. On, a person signing in on a browser they chose to remember is not asked for their second factor again within the period below of last giving it on that browser. NEVER at the admin console, the user portal or the protocol debugger; never for an administrator; never while the sign-in's risk is medium or higher; and the sign-in is then ONE factor to every relying party — amr ["pwd"] and acr "1", as a password alone — so an application asking for "mfa" is refused it. The browser is recognised by a bearer cookie: whoever copies the cookie skips the second factor too, until the copy is caught.
authn.FIELDS.rememberedBrowserDays.label: How long a remembered browser skips the second factor
authn.FIELDS.rememberedBrowserDays.what: Counted from the last time the person gave their second factor on that browser. After it they are asked again, and giving it starts the period again.

serviceAccount.FIELDS.exemptFromSecondFa: Service accounts are exempt from the second factor

OFF BY DEFAULT. On, the authentication policy's second-factor requirements do not apply to a service account in this realm, and nor does the refusal of a password alone at the password doors (#101). The account's amr still says pwd only, so a relying party asking for more is refused it. WEAKER: an account on a password alone is an account anyone with the password is.
serviceAccount.FIELDS.allowBrowserSignIn: Service accounts may sign in at a browser

OFF BY DEFAULT. Off, the sign-in screen, the user portal and the admin console refuse a service account, whichever first factor it presents, and turning a person into a service account ends their browser sessions. A service account is used by a program, and a program has no business at a sign-in screen.

kinds.passkey.label: Passkey policy
kinds.passkey.governs: how passkeys behave — whether a sign-in may name no username, and what a security key is asked to store
kinds.passkey.appliesTo: the NEXT sign-in and the NEXT passkey enrolled in this realm; a passkey already enrolled keeps what its authenticator stored
kinds.passkey.fallsBackTo: the default realm's profile where it has one, and the built-in defaults where it has not
passkey.FIELDS.allowUsernameless.label: Allow a passkey sign-in with no username
passkey.FIELDS.allowUsernameless.what: ON BY DEFAULT. On, the sign-in screen offers *Sign in with a passkey* and the username field's autofill, which ask the browser for any discoverable credential of this realm (WebAuthn Level 3 section 5.4, `allowCredentials` empty) and sign in the account its user handle names, with user verification required and checked. Off, neither is offered and a sign-in always names the person first. Replaces the setting webauthn.usernameless.
passkey.FIELDS.requireUsernameless.label: Require a passkey sign-in with no username
passkey.FIELDS.requireUsernameless.what: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, an application whose authentication mechanism is a passkey and nothing else (appAuthnMechanism `webauthn` alone) gets a sign-in screen with no username field: *Sign in with a passkey* is the way in, and a sign-in that names a person is refused. It needs the row above. The realm's `default` profile does not apply it to the admin console, the debugger or the user portal; a named profile selecting that application does.
passkey.FIELDS.securityKeyResidentKey.la: What "Use a security key" asks for while usernameless sign-in is on
passkey.FIELDS.securityKeyResidentKey.wh: The `residentKey` an enrolment through *Use a security key* (or one that names no kind) sends WHILE usernameless sign-in is ON. While it is off the button always asks `required`, so it makes a discoverable credential as *Create a passkey* does (which asks `required` always). `discouraged` or `preferred` spare a security key's few resident slots, at the cost of a key that needs the username to sign in. Replaces the setting webauthn.residentKey.
passkey.FIELDS.backupEligibility.label: Synced passkeys (backup eligible)
passkey.FIELDS.backupEligibility.what: `allow` (the default) accepts any passkey. `disallow` accepts only DEVICE-BOUND ones: a passkey whose authenticator says it may be backed up or synced (the BE flag, WebAuthn Level 3 section 6.1) is refused when it is registered and when it signs somebody in, so a synced passkey enrolled before the realm said no stops working too. BE never changes for a credential.
passkey.FIELDS.enforcePinLength.label: Require a minimum security-key PIN length
passkey.FIELDS.enforcePinLength.what: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, registration asks the authenticator for its minimum PIN length (CTAP 2.1 section 12.4, the minPinLength extension), records it on the key, and refuses a key whose minimum is below the next row, at registration and at every sign-in. A key answers only for relying parties it was configured to tell (CTAP 2.1 setMinPINLength with this RP ID); every other key, and every platform or synced passkey, does not report, and is refused unless the row after next is on.
passkey.FIELDS.minPinLength.label: Minimum security-key PIN length
passkey.FIELDS.minPinLength.what: The shortest PIN a security key may be set to accept, as the key itself reports it, while the row above is on. Between 4 (CTAP 2.1's own floor) and 63.
Accept a key that does not report its PIN length

OFF BY DEFAULT, which is the strict reading: while the PIN length is enforced, a key that does not report it is refused. On, such a key is accepted and only a reported minimum is held to the rule — so the rule then binds only keys configured to report to this relying party.
passkey.FIELDS.enforceAttestationAtSignI: Hold every sign-in to the attestation rules in force

OFF BY DEFAULT. The attestation rules (the webauthn.attestation* settings: the policy, the AAGUID list, the certification level and FIPS) are checked when a passkey is registered. On, they are checked again at every sign-in against what was recorded then and the FIDO Metadata Service as it is now, so a key registered before a rule was tightened, or whose model was since reported compromised, stops signing anybody in. A key with no trusted attestation fails every rule that demands one.
passkey.FIELDS.postQuantumRequired.label: Require a post-quantum passkey
passkey.FIELDS.postQuantumRequired.what: `off` (the default) accepts a passkey whatever its signature algorithm. `sign-in` accepts only a POST-QUANTUM passkey, one whose algorithm is ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87 (RFC 9964), when it signs somebody in, as the first credential or as the second factor; a classical one may still be registered. `registration-and-sign-in` refuses a classical one at registration too, and enrolment then offers only ML-DSA. The algorithm decides, not the lane a key was created in. Refused while the realm offers no ML-DSA (webauthn.algorithms names none, and neither webauthn.pqcOnly nor webauthn.pqcAlongsideClassical is on).
passkey.FIELDS.postQuantumAllowCredentia: Passkeys a sign-in names where a post-quantum one is required

`realm` (the default) follows the realm's webauthn.postQuantumAllowCredentials. Read only while postQuantumRequired requires a post-quantum passkey at sign-in. `narrow` names only the person's post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkeys in the passkey step's request, so a classical one is never offered, and a person whose device holds only their classical one sees the platform's own "no passkey found" message. `list-and-refuse` names every passkey they hold and refuses a classical one after the ceremony, with a page saying that this application requires a post-quantum passkey and where to add one; the person may then pick a passkey that will be refused. A person holding no post-quantum passkey is told before any ceremony either way. Left out of a save, `realm` is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.registrationAlgorithms.wh: `realm` (the default) offers the realm's webauthn.algorithms. Otherwise the signature algorithms a passkey registration offers to this profile's people, in order of preference (an authenticator makes the first it supports), from the algorithms webauthn.algorithms may name. The next row may narrow or reorder it, and a passkey whose algorithm is not one this profile offers is refused when it is registered. Left out of a save, `realm` is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.registrationMode.label: Post-quantum algorithms at registration
passkey.FIELDS.registrationMode.what: `realm` (the default) follows webauthn.pqcOnly and webauthn.pqcAlongsideClassical. `pq-only` offers only ML-DSA, and refuses a retry with the classical algorithms. `pq-first` offers ML-DSA first and the classical algorithms after it, even where the realm requests ML-DSA only. `classical-only` offers no ML-DSA and no post-quantum passkey beside a classical one, for people whose devices fail an ML-DSA registration. Refused with postQuantumRequired other than off or with attestationAlgorithms set (classical-only), and where the algorithms offered name no ML-DSA (pq-only, pq-first). Left out of a save, `realm` is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.lanes.label: A classical and a post-quantum passkey side by side
passkey.FIELDS.lanes.what: `realm` (the default) follows webauthn.pqcAlongsideClassical. `both` gives this profile's people a classical and a post-quantum passkey side by side, each under its own user handle, wherever the realm's setting is off; `one` gives them one lane wherever it is on. webauthn.pqcOnly still means one lane. Refused as `both` with registrationMode classical-only. Left out of a save, `realm` is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.clientRules.label: Clients a registration offers no ML-DSA
passkey.FIELDS.clientRules.what: EMPTY BY DEFAULT: every client is offered the list as it stands. Otherwise up to 20 rules separated by `;`, each `<browser> on <system>`, where either side is a family as the passkey ceremony rows name it (`Chrome`, `Firefox`, `macOS`, `Android`) or `*` for any, optionally followed by a major-version range (`141`, `130-140`, `130-`, `-140`): `Firefox 140- on Linux; * on Android 13`. A passkey registration from a matching client offers the list less ML-DSA (ES256 and RS256 where that leaves none). Not applied where a classical passkey is not allowed — registrationMode pq-only, webauthn.pqcOnly, postQuantumRequired registration-and-sign-in, or at the sign-in step under postQuantumRequired sign-in — nor to the post-quantum lane, and the ceremony row says it was not. Left out of a save, empty is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.passkeyHints.label: Hints "Create a passkey" sends
passkey.FIELDS.passkeyHints.what: The WebAuthn hints (Level 3 section 5.4.8) the portal's *Create a passkey* sends, in order, from security-key, client-device and hybrid, or none. They tell the browser which way of making the passkey to lead with. A hint may not contradict webauthn.authenticatorAttachment: client-device implies platform, security-key and hybrid cross-platform.
passkey.FIELDS.securityKeyHints.label: Hints "Use a security key" sends
passkey.FIELDS.securityKeyHints.what: The hints *Use a security key* sends, in order, or none. The button asks for a cross-platform authenticator, so client-device contradicts it and is refused.
passkey.FIELDS.signInHints.label: Hints a passkey sign-in sends
passkey.FIELDS.signInHints.what: The hints a sign-in ceremony sends — the passkey step, the sign-in with no username and its autofill — in order, or none (the default: the browser offers every way it knows).
passkey.FIELDS.enterpriseSerialAttribute: Directory attribute holding a person's security-key serials

EMPTY BY DEFAULT: no serial is checked. Set to an attribute of a person's entry (for example `serialNumber`, which may hold several values), a security key registers only with a TRUSTED enterprise attestation whose certificate names a device serial that is one of that person's values. Needs webauthn.attestation set to enterprise, and the vendor or platform configured to release enterprise attestation to this RP ID; without that the browser sends ordinary attestation and every registration is refused.
passkey.FIELDS.userDisplayName.label: The name a passkey prompt shows for the person
passkey.FIELDS.userDisplayName.what: EMPTY BY DEFAULT: the name the sign-in knows, else the username. Otherwise up to six directory attributes in order, separated by commas; a group of attributes separated by spaces (givenName sn) joins their values. The first whose every attribute has a value becomes user.displayName (WebAuthn Level 3 section 5.4.3), with control and direction-changing characters removed and at most 64 characters. The username is always user.name.
passkey.FIELDS.rpNameExtras.label: What a passkey prompt adds to the service's name
passkey.FIELDS.rpNameExtras.what: `none` (the default) shows webauthn.rpName alone. `realm`, `organisation` or `realm-and-organisation` append the realm's name and/or saml.organizationName, so a person with accounts in several realms can tell the prompts apart.
passkey.FIELDS.credentialLabel.label: The name a new passkey is given
passkey.FIELDS.credentialLabel.what: EMPTY BY DEFAULT: the provider's name, else "Passkey" or "Security key". Otherwise this text, with {provider} and {kind} filled in, at most 60 characters. The person may rename it afterwards, as always.
passkey.FIELDS.aggregateDevices.label: Offer a person's passkeys as one sign-in choice
passkey.FIELDS.aggregateDevices.what: ON BY DEFAULT: one "Use passkey" step whose request lists every one of the person's passkeys, and the browser offers whichever is present. Off, a person with more than one is shown a choice per passkey, by its name, and the request names only that one.
passkey.FIELDS.recoveryAssurance.label: Account recovery for a person who holds a passkey
passkey.FIELDS.recoveryAssurance.what: `any` BY DEFAULT IN DEVELOPMENT, `not-weaker` IN PRODUCT. Whether a way back into the account that asks for no passkey — a password reset link, an activation link, a recovery code, an emailed code or link — restores access for a person who holds one. `any`: at once. `not-weaker`: the first sign-in after it that is not a passkey sign-in reaches no application; the person registers a passkey that satisfies this policy and signs in with it. `operator-only`: as not-weaker, and the self-service doors (the forgot-password form, a recovery code or an emailed code or link at sign-in) are refused; only an administrator's reset link, generated password or activation link remains. Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.attestationAlgorithms.lab: Algorithms a passkey's attestation must be signed with
passkey.FIELDS.attestationAlgorithms.wha: `none` BY DEFAULT: an attestation is accepted whatever it is signed with. Otherwise a list from post-quantum, ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87, slh-dsa and composite-ml-dsa: a passkey registers only with a TRUSTED attestation that carries a certificate, whose statement signature and the signature on every certificate of its chain, from the leaf to the trust anchor, are each one the list allows (`post-quantum` allows any ML-DSA, SLH-DSA or composite ML-DSA signature). Self and none attestation are refused, having no certificate. With enforceAttestationAtSignIn on, every sign-in holds the passkey to it by what its registration recorded, so a passkey registered before the rule stops working. This is the attestation's algorithm, not the passkey's own (postQuantumRequired). Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.adminEnrolment.label: Let an administrator enrol a passkey for a person
passkey.FIELDS.adminEnrolment.what: `off` BY DEFAULT. `on` lets an administrator holding the Admin Write console role enrol a passkey for a person this profile applies to, from the person's page on the console or /admin-api: the registration ceremony runs in the administrator's own browser, against an authenticator they hold (a security key to be handed over, say), under the person's user handle, and is verified exactly as the person's own registration is — attestation, algorithms and this policy's registration rules. Nothing made elsewhere can be imported. The key records which administrator enrolled it and when, and the person is told. Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.FIELDS.deviceBoundRequired.label: Require a device-bound session
passkey.FIELDS.deviceBoundRequired.what: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, an issuance to an application this profile covers waits until the sign-on session is bound to the browser's key, and is refused when the browser skipped that registration or the wait elapsed without a binding. A session that was never offered registration is not refused by this row. Refused while authn.deviceBoundSessions is off.

The first whose every attribute has a value becomes user.displayName (WebAuthn Level 3 section 5.4.3), with control and direction-changing characters removed and at most 64 characters. The username is always user.name.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyRpNa: `none` (the default) shows webauthn.rpName alone. `realm`, `organisation` or `realm-and-organisation` append the realm's name and/or saml.organizationName, so a person with accounts in several realms can tell the prompts apart.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyCred: EMPTY BY DEFAULT: the provider's name, else "Passkey" or "Security key". Otherwise this text, with {provider} and {kind} filled in, at most 60 characters. The person may rename it afterwards, as always.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyAggr: ON BY DEFAULT: one "Use passkey" step whose request lists every one of the person's passkeys, and the browser offers whichever is present. Off, a person with more than one is shown a choice per passkey, by its name, and the request names only that one.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyReco: `any` BY DEFAULT IN DEVELOPMENT, `not-weaker` IN PRODUCT. Whether a way back into the account that asks for no passkey — a password reset link, an activation link, a recovery code, an emailed code or link — restores access for a person who holds one. `any`: at once. `not-weaker`: the first sign-in after it that is not a passkey sign-in reaches no application; the person registers a passkey that satisfies this policy and signs in with it. `operator-only`: as not-weaker, and the self-service doors (the forgot-password form, a recovery code or an emailed code or link at sign-in) are refused; only an administrator's reset link, generated password or activation link remains. Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyAtte: `none` BY DEFAULT: an attestation is accepted whatever it is signed with. Otherwise a list from post-quantum, ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87, slh-dsa and composite-ml-dsa: a passkey registers only with a TRUSTED attestation that carries a certificate, whose statement signature and the signature on every certificate of its chain, from the leaf to the trust anchor, are each one the list allows (`post-quantum` allows any ML-DSA, SLH-DSA or composite ML-DSA signature). Self and none attestation are refused, having no certificate. With enforceAttestationAtSignIn on, every sign-in holds the passkey to it by what its registration recorded, so a passkey registered before the rule stops working. This is the attestation's algorithm, not the passkey's own (postQuantumRequired). Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyAdmi: `off` BY DEFAULT. `on` lets an administrator holding the Admin Write console role enrol a passkey for a person this profile applies to, from the person's page on the console or /admin-api: the registration ceremony runs in the administrator's own browser, against an authenticator they hold (a security key to be handed over, say), under the person's user handle, and is verified exactly as the person's own registration is — attestation, algorithms and this policy's registration rules. Nothing made elsewhere can be imported. The key records which administrator enrolled it and when, and the person is told. Left out of a save, the built-in default is kept.
passkey.SCHEMA.attributes.stsPasskeyDevi: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, an issuance to an application this profile covers waits until the sign-on session is bound to the browser's key, and is refused when the browser skipped that registration or the wait elapsed without a binding. A session that was never offered registration is not refused by this row. Refused while authn.deviceBoundSessions is off.

kinds.postLogin.label: Post-login activity policy
kinds.postLogin.governs: what a person is asked to do after signing in, before they are sent back to the application — today, to register a post-quantum passkey
kinds.postLogin.appliesTo: the NEXT sign-in of every person the profile reaches in this realm; a session already started is not interrupted
kinds.postLogin.fallsBackTo: the default realm's profile where it has one, and the built-in defaults (nobody is asked anything) where it has not
postLogin.FIELDS.enabled.label: Ask after sign-in
postLogin.FIELDS.enabled.what: OFF BY DEFAULT. On, every person this profile reaches who is due the activity below is asked to do it after signing in, before they are sent back to the application. A named profile with this off EXCLUDES the members of its groups.
postLogin.FIELDS.activity.label: Activity
postLogin.FIELDS.activity.what: What is asked. pqc-passkey-migration: a person holding a passkey made with a classical algorithm as their primary sign-in, or as a second factor, is asked to register a post-quantum (ML-DSA) passkey in the same role. The classical passkey is kept. Nobody is asked where the realm offers no ML-DSA algorithm at registration (the default webauthn.algorithms does).
postLogin.FIELDS.snoozeDays.label: Skip puts it off for
postLogin.FIELDS.snoozeDays.what: How long Skip puts the activity off for that person.
postLogin.FIELDS.graceDays.label: Allotted time
postLogin.FIELDS.graceDays.what: Counted from the person's FIRST invitation. When it has passed, Skip is gone and the sign-in is held — no session is started — until the activity is done. 0 is no deadline: it can always be skipped.
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskey.label: A person with no passkey
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskey.what: leave: not asked. invite: asked to register a post-quantum passkey, and may always skip it. require: asked, and may skip it only until the allotted time has passed.
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskeyRole.label: Registered by a person with no passkey as
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskeyRole.what: primary: a passwordless sign-in. mfa: a second factor.
postLogin.FIELDS.method.label: How a classical passkey is migrated
postLogin.FIELDS.method.what: upgrade: the person uses their classical passkey once, then an ML-DSA passkey replaces it in place on the same authenticator — one passkey, nothing left behind. alongside: an ML-DSA passkey is added beside it, in the post-quantum lane where the realm offers two lanes, or on another authenticator where it offers one. automatic: alongside where the person's passkey policy offers two lanes, upgrade where it offers one.
postLogin.FIELDS.attestation.label: A passkey counts as post-quantum when
postLogin.FIELDS.attestation.what: any: its key algorithm is ML-DSA. post-quantum: its key algorithm is ML-DSA AND its recorded attestation was signed with post-quantum algorithms throughout; a passkey with a classical attestation, or none recorded, does not count, and its holder is asked for one that does.
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskeyFallback.label: A person with no passkey whose device cannot make ML-DSA
postLogin.FIELDS.noPasskeyFallback.what: none: ML-DSA only. classical: after an ML-DSA registration fails on the device, a retry with the classical algorithms is offered (where the passkey policy allows one) — a classical passkey is better than a password, and its holder is asked for the migration later like anyone else's.
